basics.name: Dr Tom Julian
basics.label: Academic Ophthalmologist
basics.summary: I am an academic ophthalmologist working at the intersection of deep learning, medical imaging, and multi-omic analyses. As a clinician with experience developing deep learning models and omics analysis pipelines, I am well positioned to lead and deliver clinically important research using advanced methods.

location.address: The Christabel Pankhurst Building, The University of Manchester, Dover St

work.name: University of Manchester & Manchester Royal Eye Hospital
work.summary: In my clinical role, I work in surgical, clinic and emergency settings at Manchester Royal Eye Hospital. In my academic role, I deliver clinically focussed research using (1) medical image analysis and (2) multi-omic analyses.

education.summary: I am currently undertaking a PhD in which I am integrating deep learning approaches (e.g. autoencoders, latent diffusion models, GANs) and omics data (e.g. genomics and metabolomics) to explore clinical questions surrounding the role of ophthalmic imaging in ocular and systemic health.
I developed skills to critically evaluate research and handle the practical and regulatory challenges of designing and conducting clinical and health research projects.

I completed my medical degree and subsequently received my license to practice as a medical doctor. During my studies, I held additional responsibilities including serving as President of Sheffield Medical Society; lecturing and small group mentorship to first year students in the MBChB programme; and serving on every Medical School Faculty steering group. In recognition of my roles, I won the Outstanding Student Contribution Award at the Annual Academic Awards (2018) and was recognised as an Associate Fellow of the Higher Education Academy (2018).

education.Grade: Distinction, with the joint-highest overall exam score in my cohort.
education.summary: I studied neurological disease and how clinical research breakthroughs are translated into treatments. I utilised my research block to undertake evidence synthesis projects.
